subjects.title: Introduction to Cyber Law and Cyber Crimes

units.title: Cyber Law Fundamentals and Legal Framework
units.topics: 1. Understanding the digital landscape, the internet, and its impact on legal systems. 2. Overview of cyberspace, networks, and communication technologies. 3. Study of the Information Technology Act (IT Act) and its amendments, Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 (DPDP Act) and other related laws. 4. Legal recognition of electronic records, digital signatures, and electronic transactions. 5. Jurisdictional issues in cyberspace.

units.title: Cyber Crimes and Digital Forensics
units.topics: 6. Comparative analysis of cyber offenses and traditional criminal offenses - Role of law enforcement agencies in cybercrime investigations. 7. Digital forensics: collecting evidence from electronic devices. 8. Types of cybercrimes: hacking, identity theft, phishing, etc. 9. Challenges in investigating and prosecuting cybercriminals. 10. Profiling cybercriminals: individuals, groups, state-sponsored actors. 11. Cybercrime courts, procedures, and challenges.

units.title: Copyright, Trademarks and Patents in Digital Realm
units.topics: 1. Copyright and Digital Content - Protection of digital works - software, music, videos, literature. Challenges in enforcing copyright online. 2. Trademarks and Domain Names - Domain name disputes and resolution mechanisms (UDRP). Trademark infringement in the digital realm. 3. Patents and Software Licensing- Patentability of software and business methods. Open-source licenses and proprietary software agreements.

units.title: Data Privacy and IPR Developments
units.topics: 4. Data Privacy and Confidentiality- Balancing innovation with privacy rights. 5. GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) and its impact on businesses. 6. Related Laws and development in IPR field with case laws.

units.title: Online Contracts and Payment Systems
units.topics: 1. Online Contracts and Consumer Protection - Formation of contracts in e-commerce transactions. 2. Consumer rights and remedies in online purchases. 3. Payment Gateways and Cybersecurity - Legal aspects of payment gateways, digital wallets, and cryptocurrencies. 4. Ensuring secure online transactions.

units.title: Intermediary Liability and Emerging Issues
units.topics: 5. Unauthorized access, data theft, and hacking and other cyber-crimes. 6. Liability of Intermediaries - Role of intermediaries (websites, ISPs, social media platforms) in content dissemination. 7. Safe harbor provisions and liability exemptions. 8. Growing Concerns Relating to Cyber Space and Cyber Technology. 9. Legal Issues Of E-Banking and Digital Payment System (with case studies).

units.title: Privacy Laws and GDPR
units.topics: 1. Introduction to Privacy Laws- concept, evolution. 2. Comparative study of privacy laws across different jurisdictions. 3. General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) - provisions, principles of data protection, rights of data subjects (access, rectification, erasure, and portability). 4. Significant data breaches and their legal aftermath.

units.title: Cross-Border Data Transfers and Emerging Technologies
units.topics: 5. Cross-Border Data Transfers and Safe Harbor Mechanisms - Challenges in transferring personal data across borders. 6. Emerging Technologies and Privacy Implications- Privacy considerations in AI, IoT, biometrics, and blockchain. 7. Balancing innovation with privacy protection. 8. Legal frameworks for regulating emerging technologies.

units.title: Journal
units.topics: a. Interactive Sessions on various legislations, Regulations and Policies on Information Technology and Cyber Law (Workshop, Seminars, Guest Lectures) and report writing of the same in the journal. (20 Marks); b. Write any 10 drafts of Legal Documents applicable in cyber law in the journal (Privacy Policy, disclaimers, cookies, user policies, etc.) (30 Marks); c. Assignment/ Project on any topic from the syllabus as decided by the subject teacher (30 Marks).

units.title: Viva voce
units.topics: Viva voce examination of 20 marks conducted by one internal faculty member and one external faculty member.

notes: One-year annual diploma program; credits not specified in syllabus text.
